**1. Aapki situation ka summary:**  
Aapne 8 July 2026 ko StyleBazaar app se ₹4,200 ke shoes order kiye the. Galat size aane par aapne 11 July ko use return kar diya aur aapke paas pickup receipt bhi hai. Company ne email par 7 dino me refund dene ko kaha tha, lekin customer care ko 3 baar call karne ke baad bhi aapka paisa wapas nahi aaya hai.

---

**2. Kanoon kya kehta hai:**  
- **Consumer definition:** Aapne online shopping ki hai, isliye aap Consumer Protection Act ke tahet consumer maane ja sakte hain.  
- **Galat samaan par refund:** E-commerce seller ko galat size ya alag samaan milne par refund dene se mana nahi karna chahiye.  
- **Refund ka samay:** Ek baar refund request accept ho jaane par online platform ko ek reasonable time (uchit samay) ke andar paisa wapas karna hota hai. Agar bill ya receipt me koi alag samay nahi likha hai, toh 30 dino ke andar refund na dena unfair trade practice (galat vyaparik tareeka) mana ja sakta hai.  
- **Grievance Officer:** Har online platform par ek Grievance Officer hona zaroori hai. Grievance Officer ko complaint ka acknowledgment 48 ghante ke andar dena hota hai aur 1 mahine ke andar samasya ka samadhan karna hota hai.

---

**3. Aapke paas kya options hain:**  
1. **StyleBazaar ke Grievance Officer ko likhein:** App ya website par Grievance Officer ke contact details dekhein. Unhe email karke order ID, pickup receipt, aur 7 dino me refund dene wali email ka screenshot attach karke bhejein.  
2. **National Consumer Helpline (NCH) me complaint karein:** Agar wahan se madad na mile, toh aap National Consumer Helpline par toll-free number 1915 (subah 8 baje se raat 8 baje tak) ya 1800114000 par call kar sakte hain. Aap WhatsApp (+918800001915) ya unki website (consumerhelpline.gov.in) ke zariye bhi apni complaint register kara sakte hain.  
3. **Formal Complaint / Consumer Court:** Agar phir bhi refund na mile, toh aap e-jagriti portal (e-jagriti.gov.in) ke zariye online complaint darj karne ka vikalp chun sakte hain.

---

**4. Kya baatein abhi unclear hain:**  
- Kya shoes aapne apne personal use ke liye kharide the ya kisi commercial purpose (vyapar) ke liye? (Personal use ke liye kharide gaye samaan par hi consumer kanoon lagu hota hai).  
- Kya StyleBazaar ki app par koi specific refund policy ya samay-seema likhi hui hai?

---

*Dhyan rakhein: Main ek AI legal assistant hoon, koi advocate nahi. Yeh sirf kanooni jankari (legal information) hai, kanooni salah (legal advice) nahi. Apne mamle par sahi salah ke liye kisi qualified lawyer se sampark karein.*

Source: Rule 4(10), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, G.S.R. 462(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: Every e-commerce entity shall effect all payments towards accepted refund requests of the consumers as prescribed by the Reserve Bank of India or any other competent authority under any law for the time being in force, within a reasonable period of time, or as prescribed under applicable laws
Plain explanation: Once a refund request is accepted, an online platform must pay it within a reasonable time, or within the time set by the Reserve Bank of India or other applicable law. This rule does not itself state a fixed number of days.

[SRC:CPA2019-S2-47-viii]
Source: Section 2(47)(viii), The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (35 of 2019)
Status: In force.
Official wording: refusing, after selling goods or rendering services, to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration thereof, if paid, within the period stipulated in the bill or cash memo or receipt or in the absence of such stipulation, within a period of thirty days
Plain explanation: Refusing to take back defective goods, or to stop deficient services, and refund the money is listed as an unfair trade practice. The time limit is the period stated in the bill or receipt. If none is stated, it is thirty days.

[SRC:ECOM2020-R4-4]
Source: Rule 4(4), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, G.S.R. 462(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: Every e-commerce entity shall establish an adequate grievance redressal mechanism having regard to the number of grievances ordinarily received by such entity from India, and shall appoint a grievance officer for consumer grievance redressal, and shall display the name, contact details, and designation of such officer on its platform
Plain explanation: Every online platform must have a way to handle complaints and must appoint a grievance officer, whose name, contact details and designation must be displayed on the platform. This is often where a written complaint can be sent first.

[SRC:ECOM2020-R6-3]
Source: Rule 6(3), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, G.S.R. 462(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: No seller offering goods or services through a marketplace e -commerce entity shall refuse to take back goods, or withdraw or discontinue services purchased or agreed to be purchased, or refuse to refund consideration, if paid, if such goods or services are defective, deficient or spurious, or if the goods or services are not of the characteristics or features as advertised or as agreed to, or if such goods or services are delivered late from the stated delivery schedule | Provided that in the case of late delivery, this sub -rule shall not be applied if such late delivery was due to force majeure
Plain explanation: A marketplace seller must not refuse to take back goods or refund the money if the goods or services are defective, deficient, spurious, different from what was advertised or agreed, or delivered late. Late delivery caused by force majeure is an exception.

[SRC:ECOM2020-R2-1]
Source: Rule 2(1), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, G.S.R. 462(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: all goods and services bought or sold over digital or electronic network including digital products | all models of e-commerce, including marketplace and inventory models of e-commerce
Plain explanation: The E-Commerce Rules apply to goods and services bought or sold online, including digital products, and to both marketplace and inventory models.

[SRC:ECOM2020-R4-5]
Source: Rule 4(5), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, G.S.R. 462(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: Every e-commerce entity shall ensure that the grievance officer referred to in sub -rule (4) acknowledges the receipt of any consumer complaint within forty -eight hours and redresses the complaint within one month from the date of receipt of the complaint
Plain explanation: A platform's grievance officer must acknowledge a consumer complaint within forty-eight hours and redress it within one month of receiving it.

[SRC:NCH-CONTACT]
Source: National Consumer Helpline: official website: Helpline contact details
Status: In force.
Official wording: Toll Free 1915 (8AM to 8PM) | WhatsApp +918800001915 | Call National Consumer Helpline at 1915 or 1800114000 | Register your consumer grievance through the NCH Web Portal, Mobile App, UMANG, WhatsApp or Call Centre.
Plain explanation: The National Consumer Helpline can be reached on toll-free 1915 (8 AM to 8 PM) or 1800114000, or on WhatsApp at +918800001915. A grievance can be registered through its web portal, mobile app, UMANG, WhatsApp or call centre.

[SRC:ECOM2020-R4-8]
Source: Rule 4(8), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, G.S.R. 462(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: No e -commerce entity shall impose cancellation charges on consumers cancelling after confirming purchase unless similar charges are also borne by the e - commerce entity, if they cancel the purchase order unilaterally for any reason
Plain explanation: An online platform cannot charge a consumer for cancelling after confirming a purchase, unless the platform also bears similar charges when it cancels an order on its own.

[SRC:ECOM2026-COMMENCEMENT]
Source: Rule 1(2), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026, G.S.R. 789(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: They shall come into force with effect from 1st January, 2027.
Plain explanation: The 2026 amendment to the E-Commerce Rules starts on 1 January 2027. Until then, the earlier wording applies.

[SRC:CPA2019-S2-7]
Source: Section 2(7), The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (35 of 2019)
Status: In force.
Official wording: the expressions “buys any goods ” and “hires or avails any services ” includes offline or online transactions through electronic means or by teleshopping or direct selling or multi-level marketing | but does not include a person who obtains such goods for resale or for any commercial purpose | the expression “commercial purpose” does not include use by a person of goods bought and used by him exclusively for the purpose of earning his livelihood, by means of self-employment
Plain explanation: A person who buys goods or pays for a service is a consumer, whether the purchase was made online or offline. Someone who buys goods to resell them or for a commercial purpose is generally not a consumer, except when the goods are used only to earn a living through self-employment.

- **Consumer definition:** Aapne online shopping ki hai, isliye aap Consumer Protection Act ke tahet consumer maane ja sakte hain.  
- **Galat samaan par refund:** E-commerce seller ko galat size ya alag samaan milne par refund dene se mana nahi karna chahiye.

1. **StyleBazaar ke Grievance Officer ko likhein:** App ya website par Grievance Officer ke contact details dekhein. Unhe email karke order ID, pickup receipt, aur 7 dino me refund dene wali email ka screenshot attach karke bhejein.
